chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the setting of the price for the fugitive slave and the stray animal, and he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الآبق: Fugitive slave who has escaped from captivity
key_terms.الجعل: Setting a price, fee, or fixed value
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on setting a price for a fugitive slave or stray animal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the permissibility of setting a fixed ransom or value for a fugitive slave (*al-abiq*) and a stray animal (*al-dhallah*) to facilitate their recovery. This ruling reflects the practical legal framework of early Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing ease in resolving property disputes and ensuring the welfare of both slaves and livestock within the community.
